svg.title: iOS · Settings · scrolled to Advanced · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/SettingsView.swift scrolled to the end of the list. The Advanced card is now tall enough that the end of the list is all Advanced — the Storage card has left the viewport entirely at this scroll depth, and the ADVANCED section header sits just under the status bar. Rows: Layout, Allow remote access (off by default), Share projects with nearby devices (off by default), Custom frame rate, Blend learning, Auto blend strategy, Dim screen during shoot, Raw decode path, Performance, Diagnostics and Incomplete Captures. Layout is the first row and the only one about the shell rather than the engine: which tabs and filters the app shows (Enable Scans menu, Display count in Projects — settings.layout.portrait.svg). Auto blend strategy is the field-test selector for BLEND=Auto's decision logic on DNG shoots (Zone / Latitude / Lumen, a menu like the Creative defaults rows); whichever is chosen, every Auto run logs all three strategies' proposals per window into capture_log.json, and the choice is per-device on purpose — a comparison shoot sets one strategy on each device. Dim screen during shoot (iOS only, ON by default) shipped with the thermal work and is drawn here for the first time. Share projects with nearby devices is the project-transfer opt-in and sits directly under Allow remote access, deliberately as a SEPARATE grant: one lets a Mac drive this camera’s shutter, the other lets it read and copy every project in the library, and the subtitle says the part that matters — the pairing code is not per-project. Switching it on arms Shared/ProjectTransferServer.swift the next time the Projects tab appears and puts the sharing chip in that header (projects.sharing.portrait.svg); switching it off stands the listener down at once, so a code cannot be left advertising from a phone in a bag. Adding it pushed every row below it down 81pt, so Diagnostics is now the last row this scroll position reaches; Performance and Incomplete Captures are unchanged and still specified above. Raw decode path is the second field-test selector and takes the same menu shape as Auto blend strategy: it chooses how a DNG is rendered before grading — Bradford (default: white balance as a 3×3 in linear Display P3, after Apple's camera profile), Forward matrix (the same insertion point, but the matrix comes from the DNG's own calibration tags), Core Image RAW (white balance inside the raw converter, in camera space before the profile — Lightroom's ordering), and Adobe DCP (Core Image RAW's ordering plus the camera's Adobe profile look table). The first three are all arguments about which 3×3 goes where, so they render identically while temperature and tint sit at zero and none of them can change an untouched project. Adobe DCP is the exception on both counts, and the row's copy no longer claims otherwise: a look table moves hue differently at different brightnesses — which is the whole reason it exists, and the one thing no 3×3 can imitate — so it applies whatever the sliders say and does change an untouched render. Changing any of them invalidates every cached preview. Adobe DCP is also the only case that can be unavailable, and on iPhone it always is: the profiles ship with Lightroom/Camera Raw and there is no /Library/Application Support/Adobe on a phone, so the row is permanently listed-but-disabled here (it is live on a Mac that has them, which is where the field test runs). It now carries the reason — "Adobe camera profiles are not installed. They ship with Lightroom or Camera Raw" — rather than a bare "(unavailable)", so a greyed row is not read as an unfinished feature. That label is inside the menu, which no file in this folder draws for either field-test row. The last row exists only while orphaned capture logs do: CaptureSessionLogger deletes a session's log when the capture screen closes normally, so a surviving log means the app died with the camera open, and the row's trailing number is CaptureSessionLogger.orphanedLogs.count. With no orphans the row is absent and Diagnostics is the card's last row (no divider under it). Tapping opens the Incomplete Captures sheet — settings.incomplete-captures.portrait.svg. The list's trailing 96pt spacer is what leaves the last row clear of the floating tab bar, which floats over the scroll.
